kms.policy-editor.addFromAttestationDesc: This writes an <0>explicit Deny</0> (one per selected PCR) for any request whose NitroTPM PCRs are missing or different. No Allow is added — the base decrypt permission already comes from the key's root/IAM delegation, and the explicit Deny overrides all Allows, so it is what actually enforces "decrypt only inside an attested instance."

kms.policy-editor.consistencyNoCondition: KMS policy has NO attestation conditions — decryption is not gated on any PCR yet
kms.policy-editor.enforcedByDeny: <0>Enforced by an explicit Deny.</0> Applying conditions writes an explicit <1>Deny</1> on <2>kms:Decrypt</2> (one per PCR) for any request whose NitroTPM PCRs are missing or different. No extra Allow is added — the base permission already comes from the key's root/IAM delegation, and in IAM/KMS evaluation an explicit Deny overrides every Allow. So the data can be decrypted <3> only</3> inside an instance presenting these exact measurements, even if another policy would otherwise allow it.
kms.policy-editor.enforcedNote: Only the PCRs bound in the KMS policy are enforced. A “not enforced” row is a measured PCR you chose not to bind (e.g. PCR0) — informational, not an error. A blank column means that source has no value for that PCR.

predictions.job-history.structureDescrip: This is the predicted folded shape of your <0>single input protein</0> — the model infers where each amino acid sits in 3D. It is <1>not</1> a docking or binding result: there is no second molecule, no DNA/RNA, and no binding-affinity calculation. The ribbon is colored from the start of the chain (blue) to the end (red) to help you trace the backbone; the colors carry no other meaning. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.

predictions.job-history.whatThisPredicts: Given <0>one protein sequence</0>, the Boltz-1 model predicts its<1> 3D folded structure</1> (where each amino acid sits in space) and returns a downloadable PDB plus a structure-confidence score (pLDDT). It does <2>not</2> do docking, protein–protein / protein–DNA complexes, or binding-affinity prediction.
